title: M0.1: Scaffold Tauri 2 project with React + TypeScript
description:
## Goal
Scaffold a new Tauri 2 project with React + TypeScript template using pnpm.

## What to do
1. Run: pnpm create tauri-app
   - Project name: qtranslate
   - Template: React + TypeScript
   - Package manager: pnpm
2. Verify the project structure is created correctly
3. Verify pnpm tauri dev runs and shows an empty window
4. Verify pnpm tauri build produces an artifact

## Files created by template
- src/ (React frontend)
- src-tauri/ (Rust backend)
- package.json
- Cargo.toml
- tauri.conf.json
- vite.config.ts
- tsconfig.json
- index.html

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] pnpm tauri dev launches and shows empty window
- [ ] pnpm tauri build produces a .exe file on Windows
- [ ] Project has standard Tauri 2 structure
- [ ] No errors in console during dev mode

## Background
This is the foundation for the entire QTranslate clone project. We use Tauri 2 because:
1. Cross-platform support (Windows + macOS)
2. Rust backend for avoiding CORS issues with translation APIs
3. Native OS integration (hotkeys, clipboard, input simulation)
4. Small binary size compared to Electron

## Time estimate: 30 minutes

title: M0.2: Setup dependencies and project structure
description:
## Goal
Install all required dependencies and create the full project directory structure.

## Rust crates to install (in src-tauri/ directory)
Run these commands in src-tauri/:
- cargo add tauri-plugin-global-shortcut: Cross-platform global hotkeys
- cargo add enigo@0.2.1: Keyboard input simulation. CRITICAL: Must be 0.2+, NOT 0.1.x or older
- cargo add arboard: Cross-platform clipboard read/write
- cargo add reqwest: HTTP client for translation API (avoids CORS in webview)
- cargo add serde serde_json: Serialization for settings and API responses
- cargo add tokio: Async runtime (if not already included by Tauri)

## npm packages to install (in project root)
- pnpm add zustand: Lightweight state management (MVI pattern)
- pnpm add @tauri-apps/plugin-global-shortcut: TypeScript bindings for global shortcut plugin
- pnpm add @tauri-apps/api: Tauri API bindings (may already be included)

## Directory structure to create
src/
  components/ (Header, SourcePanel, TranslationToolbar, ResultPanel, ProviderBar, QuickTranslatePopup, LanguageSelector, LoadingSpinner)
  services/ (translation, clipboard, selectionCapture, history, settings)
  stores/ (translationStore, settingsStore)
  domain/ (language, translation, settings)
  providers/ (google, deepl, microsoft, openai)
  styles/ (app.css, popup.css, themes.css)

src-tauri/src/
  commands/ (mod, clipboard, selection, input, translate, window, settings)
  permissions.rs

## Dev tooling setup
- ESLint for TypeScript linting
- Prettier for code formatting
- Vitest for TypeScript unit tests

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All Rust crates installed and compile (cargo build in src-tauri/)
- [ ] All npm packages installed
- [ ] Directory structure created
- [ ] pnpm tauri dev still works after adding dependencies
- [ ] No compilation errors

## Important Notes
- enigo MUST be 0.2+ (check Cargo.toml). Old API (key_sequence_parse) is removed.
- Pin enigo version explicitly: enigo = { version = "0.2.1", features = [...] }
- If cargo build fails, check crate versions and features.

## Time estimate: 1 hour

title: M0.2b: Tauri 2 Capabilities/Permissions configuration
description:
## Goal
Configure Tauri 2 capabilities/permissions. This is CRITICAL and commonly forgotten.

## Why this matters
Tauri 2 defaults to DENY-ALL. If permissions are not declared, every command/window/shortcut call fails with 'not allowed' even if Rust code is correct. This is the #1 debugging time-waster for new Tauri 2 projects.

## File: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json
Must declare all permissions:

{
  "identifier": "default",
  "description": "Default permissions for the app",
  "windows": ["main"],
  "permissions": [
    "core:default",
    "global-shortcut:allow-register",
    "global-shortcut:allow-unregister",
    "global-shortcut:allow-is-registered",
    "window:default",
    "window:allow-create",
    "window:allow-show",
    "window:allow-hide",
    "window:allow-set-position",
    "window:allow-set-size",
    "window:allow-set-focus",
    "shell:allow-open",
    "YOUR-CUSTOM-COMMANDS-HERE"
  ]
}

## Custom commands to add
After implementing each Rust command, add its permission:
- translate-text
- get-selected-text
- replace-with-translation
- backup-clipboard
- restore-clipboard
- load-settings
- save-settings
- check-accessibility-permission (macOS only)

## Also: tauri.conf.json plugins section
Must register tauri-plugin-global-shortcut:
{
  "plugins": {
    "global-shortcut": {}
  }
}

## Testing
After setup, test with a simple command to verify permissions work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] capabilities/default.json exists with all required permissions
- [ ] No 'not allowed' errors when testing commands
- [ ] tauri.conf.json has global-shortcut plugin registered
- [ ] Custom command permissions added as commands are implemented

## Background
Without this step, M2a commands will fail silently with permission errors that look like logic bugs. Do this NOW in M0.2 so M2a works immediately.

## Time estimate: 30 minutes

title: M0.3: Verify build pipeline
description:
## Goal

2. Run pnpm tauri build — must produce .exe on Windows

4. Run pnpm test — TypeScript tests must pass

title: M1.1: TypeScript domain models (LanguageCode, TranslationRequest/Response/Error)
description:
## Goal
Define the core domain models in TypeScript that will be used throughout the app.

## Files to create

### src/domain/language.ts
- LanguageCode type with constants: AUTO, ENGLISH, VIETNAMESE, JAPANESE, CHINESE, KOREAN, FRENCH, GERMAN, SPANISH, etc.
- Regex validation for BCP-47 tags: ^[a-zA-Z]{2,8}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,8})*$ or 'auto'
- toDisplayName() helper for UI display

### src/domain/translation.ts
- TranslationRequest: { text: string, sourceLanguage: LanguageCode, targetLanguage: LanguageCode }
- TranslationResponse: { translatedText: string, detectedLanguage?: LanguageCode, alternatives?: string[] }
- TranslationError: { code: string, message: string, retryable: boolean }

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] LanguageCode type with all constants defined
- [ ] BCP-47 validation works
- [ ] TranslationRequest/Response/Error types defined
- [ ] Unit tests pass for validation

## Background
These models are the contract between TypeScript and Rust. The Rust side returns TranslationResult (Serialize), TypeScript maps it to TranslationResponse. Keeping models clean ensures type safety across the FFI boundary.

title: M1.2: Rust translation command (translate.rs with reqwest)
description:
## Goal
Implement the Rust-side translation command that performs HTTP calls to Google's unofficial API.

## CRITICAL: Why Rust, not TypeScript
Google's unofficial endpoints have NO CORS headers. fetch() in Tauri webview gets blocked. Rust reqwest HTTP client is not subject to CORS restrictions.

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/translate.rs

## CRITICAL: Response parsing
Do NOT use #[derive(Deserialize)] structs for translate_a/single response. The response has inconsistent nested types. Use serde_json::Value:



## 2 Endpoints (separate parsers, NO simple fallback)

### Primary: translate.googleapis.com/translate_a/single
Query params: client=gtx, sl=source, tl=target, dt=t, dt=bd, dt=at, dt=ex, dt=ld, dt=md, dt=rw, dt=rm, dt=ss, dt=qc, q=text
Response: nested array [[['translated','source',...],...],...,'en']

### Fallback: clients5.google.com/translate_a/t
Query params: client=dict-chrome-ex, sl=source, tl=target, q=text
Response: {sentences:[{text:'...'}], src:'en'}

## Tauri command
#[tauri::command]
async fn translate_text(text: String, source_lang: String, target_lang: String) -> Result<TranslationResult, String>

## Error handling
- Network errors -> retryable
- Rate limiting -> retryable with backoff
- Invalid response -> not retryable
- Timeout -> retryable (10 second timeout)

## Test with curl first
Test the endpoints manually before implementing:
curl 'https://translate.googleapis.com/translate_a/single?client=gtx&sl=en&tl=vi&dt=t&q=Hello'

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] translate_text command compiles
- [ ] Primary endpoint parsing works
- [ ] Fallback endpoint parsing works
- [ ] Error handling covers network, rate limit, timeout
- [ ] cargo test passes for parsing functions
- [ ] Command registered in capabilities/default.json

## Time estimate: 3-4 hours

title: M1.3: TranslationProvider contract and Google provider (TypeScript)
description:
## Goal
Define the TranslationProvider interface and implement the Google provider as a thin TypeScript wrapper that calls the Rust backend via Tauri invoke.

## Files to create

### src/providers/translation-provider.ts
interface TranslationProvider {
  readonly key: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly supportedLanguages: LanguageCode[];
  translate(request: TranslationRequest): Promise<TranslationResponse>;
  validate(): Promise<boolean>;
}

### src/providers/google.ts
- Implements TranslationProvider
- Does NOT call fetch() directly (CORS blocked)
- Calls Rust backend: invoke('translate_text', { text, sourceLang, targetLang })
- Returns mapped TranslationResponse

### src/services/translation.ts
- translate(request, provider?) — translate with default or specified provider
- getAvailableProviders() — list of providers
- setActiveProvider(key) — switch provider

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TranslationProvider interface defined
- [ ] GoogleProvider implements interface, calls invoke()
- [ ] TranslationService orchestrates providers
- [ ] Unit tests pass for provider wrapper

## Background
TypeScript layer is intentionally thin. All HTTP happens in Rust (reqwest). TypeScript just maps types and calls invoke(). This keeps the architecture clean while avoiding CORS issues.

title: M2a.1: Global hotkey Ctrl+Q via tauri-plugin-global-shortcut
description:
## Goal
Register Ctrl+Q as a global hotkey using tauri-plugin-global-shortcut.

## File: src-tauri/src/main.rs

## Implementation
Use tauri_plugin_global_shortcut::Builder to register the shortcut:
- Register 'CmdOrCtrl+Q'
- On trigger, emit 'quick-translate' event to React frontend
- Check register result — if shortcut is taken by another app, log warning

## Important notes
- Ctrl+Q commonly conflicts (many apps use Ctrl+Q for quit/quick action)
- register() may fail silently if shortcut is taken
- Log warning on failure, show notification suggesting hotkey change (M4)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ctrl+Q triggers 'quick-translate' event
- [ ] Register failure is logged with warning
- [ ] Event reaches React frontend

## Background
Global hotkey is the entry point for the entire Quick Translate workflow. Using tauri-plugin-global-shortcut avoids writing platform-specific RegisterHotKey/CGEventTap code.

title: M2a.2: Selection capture via clipboard simulation (enigo + arboard)
description:
## Goal
Capture selected text from any app using clipboard simulation.

## CRITICAL: This is NOT direct selection reading
No OS API can read text selected in another app. The technique used by all clipboard-translators:
1. Backup current clipboard (arboard)
2. Simulate Ctrl+C (enigo 0.2+ API)
3. Poll clipboard for change (up to 200ms timeout)
4. Read clipboard - this is the selected text
5. Restore original clipboard

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/selection.rs

## No-selection detection
If user presses Ctrl+Q without selecting anything, clipboard won't change.
Must detect clipboard_after == clipboard_before and return error.
Otherwise the app silently translates old clipboard content (looks like it works but is garbage).

## Concurrency guard
If user presses Ctrl+Q twice quickly while first translation is in-flight,
two backup/simulate-copy/restore flows run concurrently and corrupt clipboard.

Use AtomicBool in Tauri managed state:


At start: compare_exchange(false, true) - skip if already running
At end (in drop or finally): store(false)

## enigo 0.2+ API (CRITICAL - old API removed)


## Clipboard polling


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] get_selected_text command works
- [ ] Clipboard backed up before capture
- [ ] Clipboard restored after capture
- [ ] No-selection detected and returns error
- [ ] Concurrency guard prevents double-trigger
- [ ] enigo 0.2+ API used (not old key_sequence_parse)

## Time estimate: 4-6 hours

title: M2a.3: Clipboard backup/restore commands
description:
## Goal
Implement clipboard backup and restore commands for safe clipboard manipulation.

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/clipboard.rs

## Commands
async fn backup_clipboard() -> Result<Option<String>, String>
async fn restore_clipboard(content: Option<String>) -> Result<(), String>

## Why this is mandatory
Without backup/restore, the app would overwrite user's clipboard content. For example:
1. User copies a URL
2. Presses Ctrl+Q
3. App captures selection (overwrites clipboard)
4. User pastes somewhere — gets translation instead of URL

With backup/restore:
1. User copies a URL
2. Presses Ctrl+Q
3. App backs up URL, captures selection, translates, restores URL
4. User pastes somewhere — still gets URL

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] backup_clipboard returns current clipboard content
- [ ] restore_clipboard restores previous content
- [ ] Works with text content
- [ ] Handles empty clipboard gracefully

## Background
Clipboard management is the trickiest part of this app. Every clipboard operation must be paired with a restore to avoid disrupting user's workflow.

title: M2a.4: Popup window (create once at startup, non-focus-stealing)
description:
## Goal
Create the translation popup window that appears on Ctrl+Q.

## CRITICAL: Create window ONCE at startup
Do NOT create a new window per Ctrl+Q. That would:
- Be slow (native window spawn each time)
- Require re-applying WS_EX_NOACTIVATE every time
- Ruin instant translate UX

## Flow
App start -> create hidden popup window -> Ctrl+Q -> update content + reposition + show -> Escape/click outside -> hide (do NOT destroy)

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/window.rs

## Non-focus-stealing (Windows)
Requires WS_EX_NOACTIVATE. Tauri WindowBuilder does not expose this directly.
Need raw-window-handle to set extended style after window creation (only once, at startup).

Implementation approach:
1. Create window with Tauri
2. Get raw window handle
3. Set WS_EX_NOACTIVATE via Windows API
4. Store window handle in managed state for reuse

## Positioning
- Display near text selection (if cursor position can be detected)
- Multi-monitor support (use monitor info from Tauri)
- DPI scaling (use scale_factor from monitor)
- Stay within screen bounds

## Window properties
- Width: 350px (adjustable based on content)
- Height: 150px (auto-size based on content)
- Always on top
- Not focusable (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE)
- Frameless (optional, for cleaner look)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Popup window created once at startup (hidden)
- [ ] WS_EX_NOACTIVATE set correctly on Windows
- [ ] Window shows/hides on command
- [ ] Content updates without recreating window
- [ ] Window positioned correctly near cursor
- [ ] Multi-monitor support works
- [ ] DPI scaling works

## Time estimate: 4-6 hours (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE is tricky)

title: M2a.6: Translation store (MVI pattern with Zustand)
description:
## Goal
Implement the MVI state management for translation using Zustand.

## File: src/stores/translationStore.ts

## State
{ inputText, translatedText, isLoading, error, sourceLang, targetLang }

## Intents (actions)
- TRANSLATE: trigger translation
- SHOW_POPUP: show popup with text
- HIDE_POPUP: hide popup
- COPY_RESULT: copy translation to clipboard
- SET_ERROR: set error state
- CLEAR: reset state

## Pattern
State -> Intent -> Reducer -> New State
Zustand handles this with create() and set()

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Store created with all state fields
- [ ] All intents implemented
- [ ] State updates correctly for each intent
- [ ] Loading state managed properly

## Background
MVI pattern keeps state management predictable and testable. Zustand is lightweight and TypeScript-first, perfect for this use case.

title: M2a.7: End-to-end wiring (Ctrl+Q -> capture -> translate -> popup)
description:
## Goal
Wire together all M2a components for end-to-end Ctrl+Q functionality.

## Flow
1. User presses Ctrl+Q
2. tauri-plugin-global-shortcut emits quick-translate event
3. React receives event via listen()
4. Call get_selected_text (clipboard simulation)
5. Handle error: if 'No text selected', show message, stop
6. Call translate_text (Rust backend)
7. Handle error: show error in popup
8. Update translation store
9. Show popup with result

## Files involved
- src-tauri/src/main.rs (hotkey handler + event emission)
- src-tauri/src/commands/selection.rs (get_selected_text)
- src-tauri/src/commands/translate.rs (translate_text)
- src/stores/translationStore.ts (state management)
- src/components/QuickTranslatePopup.tsx (UI)

## Error handling
- No selection -> show 'No text selected' in popup (brief)
- Network error -> show error with retry button
- Translation error -> show error message
- All errors -> clipboard restored, no data loss

## Performance target
- Ctrl+Q to popup visible: < 500ms
- Translation latency: depends on network (100-2000ms typical)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ctrl+Q triggers full flow
- [ ] Selected text captured correctly
- [ ] Translation returned and displayed
- [ ] Popup shows with result
- [ ] Clipboard restored after capture
- [ ] Error states handled (no selection, network error)
- [ ] Performance acceptable (< 500ms to popup)

## Time estimate: 3-4 hours

12. Select text -> Ctrl+Q -> clipboard restored after capture

title: M2b.1: macOS Accessibility permission check
description:
## Goal
Implement macOS Accessibility permission detection and user guidance.

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/permissions.rs

## Why this is required
macOS requires Accessibility permission to simulate keypresses (Ctrl+C/V).
Without it, all key simulation commands fail silently.
The app literally cannot function without this permission.

## Implementation
Use AXIsProcessTrusted() from ApplicationServices framework:

#[tauri::command]
async fn check_accessibility_permission() -> Result<bool, String> {
    let trusted = unsafe { AXIsProcessTrusted() };
    Ok(trusted != 0)
}

## If not granted - CRITICAL: show clear guidance
Do NOT just return false. Must show user-facing message:
'App needs Accessibility permission to read text selection.
Go to System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Accessibility -> add this app.'

## Link to open System Settings
open 'x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Accessibility'

## When to check
- On app startup (before registering hotkeys)
- When Ctrl+Q is pressed and permission not granted
- Show guidance dialog, not just console error

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] check_accessibility_permission returns correct status
- [ ] User guidance shown when permission not granted
- [ ] Link opens System Settings correctly
- [ ] App does not silently fail
- [ ] Guidance dialog is clear and actionable

## Time estimate: 2-3 hours

title: M3a.1: Ctrl+Alt+W hotkey for replace translation
description:
## Goal
Register Ctrl+Alt+W as global hotkey for replace translation.

## Why Ctrl+Alt+W (not Ctrl+W or Alt+W)
- Ctrl+W = universal close-tab/close-window (browser, VS Code, etc.)
- Alt+W = Windows menu accelerator (would hijack Window menu in all apps with menu bars)
- Ctrl+Alt+W = uncommon enough to avoid conflicts

## Implementation
Use tauri-plugin-global-shortcut to register 'CmdOrCtrl+Alt+W'
On trigger, emit 'replace-hotkey-pressed' event

## Important
If Ctrl+Alt+W conflicts in practice, move hotkey customization to M4 (sooner than planned).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ctrl+Alt+W registered as global hotkey
- [ ] Event emitted on trigger
- [ ] No conflicts with common apps

## Background
Replace translation is the second core feature. Hotkey choice is critical — wrong choice means constant conflicts and poor UX.

title: M3a.2: Full replace flow (capture -> translate -> paste -> restore)
description:
## Goal
Implement the complete replace translation flow as a single Tauri command.

## File: src-tauri/src/commands/input.rs + translate.rs

## Flow (single command - all steps atomic)
1. Concurrency guard (AtomicBool) - skip if another operation running
2. Backup clipboard (arboard)
3. Capture selection (Ctrl+C sim + clipboard read)
4. Translate (reqwest -> Google API)
5. Set clipboard = translated text
6. Simulate Ctrl+V (enigo 0.2+ API)
7. Wait 150ms (for paste to complete in target app)
8. Restore original clipboard

## CRITICAL: Safety rules
- If translation fails at any step -> Err returned, clipboard restored, no text lost
- Read-only field handling: if Ctrl+V fails (PDF viewer, disabled input), detect by re-reading clipboard - if still contains translated text, log warning. No crash, graceful silent fail.

## Clipboard delay
150ms is starting point. For long text or apps with heavy paste processing (Word autoformat), may need 200ms+. Test with long paragraphs and adjust.

## Error handling
- Capture failed -> restore clipboard, return error
- Translation failed -> restore clipboard, return error
- Paste failed -> restore clipboard, log warning (read-only field)
- All errors -> original text preserved, no data loss

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Full flow works end-to-end
- [ ] Translation fails -> original text preserved
- [ ] Original clipboard restored after replace
- [ ] Read-only field -> graceful fail, no crash
- [ ] Concurrency guard prevents double-trigger
- [ ] enigo 0.2+ API used correctly
- [ ] 150ms delay works for most cases

## Time estimate: 4-6 hours

title: M3a.4: React replace handler and wiring
description:
## Goal

3. Call replace_with_translation (full flow in Rust)
4. Update store with result
5. Show brief feedback (optional — no popup for replace)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] React correctly handles the event
- [ ] Store updated with replace result

## Background

title: M3a.5: Test Ctrl+Alt+W on multiple Windows apps
description:
## Goal
Manually test Ctrl+Alt+W replace translation on multiple Windows applications.

## Test matrix (run in order)

### Basic functionality
1. Notepad: type 'Hello world' -> select -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> text replaced with translation
2. Chrome: navigate to textarea -> select text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> text replaced
3. VS Code: open file -> select text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> text replaced

### Edge cases
4. Word: select text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> text replaced (check autoformat)
5. Multiline: select multi-line text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> replaced correctly
6. Long text: select paragraph -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> replaced (check clipboard delay)
7. Unicode: select Vietnamese text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> replaced with English

### Error handling
8. Disconnect internet -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> original text preserved
9. Select text in read-only field (PDF viewer) -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> graceful fail, no crash

### Clipboard
10. Copy something to clipboard -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> paste original elsewhere -> original still there
11. Select text -> Ctrl+Alt+W -> clipboard restored after replace

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 11 test cases pass
- [ ] Replace is accurate
- [ ] Original text preserved on failure
- [ ] Clipboard restored correctly
- [ ] Read-only fields handled gracefully
- [ ] No crashes or hangs

Document the failure with details. Fix issues before proceeding to M3b (macOS).

title: M4: Independent language config + hotkey customization
description:
## Goal
Allow Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+Alt+W to have independent language configurations. Make hotkeys configurable.

## Files to create/modify
- src/domain/settings.ts: Config types
- src-tauri/src/commands/settings.rs: Load/save settings
- src/stores/settingsStore.ts: Settings state management

## Config structure
QuickTranslateConfig {
  sourceLanguage: LanguageCode (default: auto)
  targetLanguage: LanguageCode (default: vi)
  hotkey: string (default: CmdOrCtrl+Q)
}

ReplaceConfig {
  sourceLanguage: LanguageCode (default: auto)
  targetLanguage: LanguageCode (default: en)
  hotkey: string (default: CmdOrCtrl+Alt+W)
}

AppSettings {
  quickTranslate: QuickTranslateConfig
  replace: ReplaceConfig
  activeProvider: string (default: google)
}

## Why independent configs
Users have different workflows:
- Ctrl+Q: Japanese -> Vietnamese (reading foreign text)
- Ctrl+Alt+W: Vietnamese -> English (writing in English)

## Hotkey re-registration
When user changes hotkey in settings:
1. Unregister old hotkey
2. Register new hotkey
3. Handle conflict detection
4. Save to settings file

## Settings UI (simple)
- Dropdown for source language
- Dropdown for target language
- Hotkey input field
- Save/Cancel buttons

- [ ] Ctrl+Q uses its own config
- [ ] Ctrl+Alt+W uses its own config
- [ ] Hotkeys configurable via settings
- [ ] Settings persist to file
- [ ] Settings reload on restart
- [ ] Hotkey re-registration works

title: M7: Native desktop reliability (hotkeys, clipboard, tray)
description:
## Goal
Make hotkeys, clipboard, and selection work reliably on Windows + macOS.

## Tasks

### 1. Hotkey conflict handling
- Detect when register() fails (shortcut taken by another app)
- Show notification: 'Ctrl+Q is already used by another app. Change shortcut in Settings?'
- Log warning with details
- Provide fallback: suggest alternative hotkey

### 2. Clipboard edge cases
- Handle clipboard lock (another app holding clipboard open)
- Handle clipboard change detection (poll for changes)
- Handle binary content in clipboard (images, files - skip, only handle text)
- Handle very large text (limit to 10,000 characters?)

### 3. Selection capture robustness
- Test on many apps (browsers, editors, terminals, etc.)
- Handle protected content (DRM, security software blocking Ctrl+C)
- Handle different text encodings (UTF-8, UTF-16, etc.)
- Handle empty selection gracefully (return clear error)

### 4. System tray
- Tray icon (use Tauri tray API)
- Right-click menu: Show/Hide window, Settings, Quit
- Minimize to tray on close (optional, configurable)

### 5. Single instance
- Only one instance running at a time
- Second instance -> focus existing window
- Use Tauri single instance plugin or custom implementation

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hotkey conflicts handled gracefully
- [ ] Clipboard edge cases covered
- [ ] Selection works on 5+ different apps
- [ ] System tray functional
- [ ] Single instance enforced
- [ ] No crashes or hangs in edge cases

title: M8: Multiple translation providers (DeepL, Microsoft, OpenAI)
description:
## Goal

title: M10: Extended features (OCR, TTS, Dictionary, Summarize)
description:
## Goal
Add advanced features beyond basic translation.

## Features

### 1. OCR (Optical Character Recognition)
- Screen capture -> image -> extract text -> translate
- Use Tesseract.js or native OCR
- Trigger: button in UI or hotkey
- Flow: capture screen region -> OCR -> show extracted text -> translate

### 2. TTS (Text-to-Speech)
- Play translated text audio
- Use Web Speech API or native TTS
- Trigger: speaker icon in popup
- Support multiple voices/languages

### 3. Dictionary
- Word lookup with definitions and examples
- Use Wiktionary API or similar
- Trigger: double-click word or dedicated button
- Show: definition, examples, synonyms

### 4. Summarize/Rewrite
- OpenAI integration for text transformation
- Summarize: condense long text
- Rewrite: change style/tone
- Trigger: dedicated buttons in UI

## Implementation notes
- Each feature is independent
- Can be implemented incrementally
- Each needs its own Tauri command (for API calls)
- Each needs UI component

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OCR captures and translates screen text
- [ ] TTS plays pronunciation
- [ ] Dictionary provides word definitions
- [ ] Summarize condenses long text
- [ ] Rewrite transforms text style
- [ ] Each feature works independently

## Time estimate: 12-16 hours (all features combined)
